content:
CONFIRMED

Evidence:

- Every SQLite session save unconditionally calls `replaceTimelineProjection(session.document())` at `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:213-224`.
- `replaceTimelineProjection` calls `document.entries()`, filters, and materializes the complete message list before querying `timelineSize` or taking the unchanged-size early return at the same file, lines 437-452.
- `SessionDocument.entries()` replays the full mutation log. `replay(...)` sorts/traverses all mutations and allocates projection collections at `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-session-api\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\session\tree\SessionDocument.java:1001-1003,1646-1712`.
- Saves are triggered by any aggregate state change, not only transcript changes: `PersistentHostStore.saveIfChanged` compares queue, commands, events, composer configuration, and active-run configuration at `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\PersistentHostStore.java:253-293`.
- Confirmed non-transcript mutation paths include composer updates, queue reorder/promote/remove/resume, command reservation/release, and run-config lifecycle changes. Thus repeated mutations incur cumulative full-history projection work.
- Additionally, every save unconditionally rebuilds the search projection and invokes `document.entries()` again at `SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:223,527-552`, further increasing the cost.
